name: Branchial Gill System
description: Introduces functional gill structures in the neck — three pairs of branchial slits with vascularized gill filaments capable of extracting dissolved oxygen from water. The gills are supplementary to lung breathing; the user can breathe air normally and switch to gill respiration when submerged. The gill slits are visible — vertical openings along the sides of the neck that flex with each breath-cycle when submerged. On land, they close to thin lines that are noticeable but not immediately alarming. Crucible Genomics' full installation includes enhanced skin moisture retention to prevent gill desiccation in dry environments. The modification enables indefinite underwater breathing in oxygenated water. In GLMZ's polluted harbor, water quality limits practical gill-breathing to 2–3 hours before the filtration capacity of the gills is overwhelmed by contaminants. The modification is rare, expensive, and visually dramatic — gill users are immediately identifiable.
source_organism: Ambystoma mexicanum (axolotl, external gill architecture), Protopterus annectens (West African lungfish, air-water transition genes)
procedure: Cervical surgery with retroviral gill tissue induction, 3 surgical sessions over 2 months
reversibility: Surgically removable; leaves significant neck scarring
side_effects: Gill slits visible on neck — cannot be hidden without high collars
Gills must be kept moist — dry environments cause irritation and cracking
Vulnerability to waterborne pathogens through gill tissue
Neck mobility slightly reduced by gill musculature
Social stigma from visible radical modification
social_perception: A line-crossing modification. Gills mark the user as someone who has moved beyond cosmetic self-expression into functional human redesign. Reactions range from fascination to disgust. In Old Harbor, gill users form a tight community. Elsewhere, they face discrimination.
story_hooks: A gill user discovers an underwater community living in the flooded sub-basements of a collapsed district — people who went aquatic years ago and never came back up
A Crucible Genomics gill installation includes a hidden genetic payload that makes the user dependent on a specific water additive — creating biological brand loyalty
